name: MRBench and the BEA 2025 shared task data
summary: Replies from seven AI and human tutors to students' math mistakes, each annotated on eight teaching dimensions, such as finding the mistake, revealing the answer and giving actionable guidance.
grades: not stated (elementary and middle school problems, from Bridge and MathDial)

license.note: Stated in the README; there is no LICENSE file. Its dialogues come from MathDial and Bridge, and Bridge's dataset card says CC BY-NC 4.0, so whether its data may be used commercially is unclear.

made_by: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
cite: Maurya, K. K., Srivatsa, K. A., Petukhova, K., & Kochmar, E. (2025). Unifying AI Tutor Evaluation: An Evaluation Taxonomy for Pedagogical Ability Assessment of LLM-Powered AI Tutors. NAACL 2025. https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2025.naacl-long.57

fits.how: Its annotations are a set to check a judge against: how far it agrees with people on guidance, on finding the mistake and on what to do next, as the harness's judge calibration does with a teacher's labels.

connect.note: Checks your judge model against trained annotators, with no labels of your own, on tutors' replies to learners' math mistakes: confusion table, agreement and kappa, half Yes and half No. It describes this model on these replies and this rubric (--dimension), not your agent. Its license is unclear for commercial use: asks you to accept it first. These are real tutoring conversations from its sources: running this sends them to the model you name, so use one whose terms you accept.
